source_line: HubSpot portal 4451852 · CRM contacts + Marketing Email Analytics API
intro_html: Built directly from HubSpot's CRM API and marketing-email analytics, contact-level lifecycle stages, nurture-track properties, and per-email send data, as an independent read alongside Tim's own workflow-reporting build. Every section on this page was pulled fresh on Oct 13, 2026. Lifecycle movement is measured from Aug 18, the date the program went live per the Asana launch milestone.

lifecycle.note_html: "Scratch everything else, lifecycle stage movement is the top metric." Contacts currently tagged into a Fall 2026 nurture track whose lifecyclestage advanced (entered MQL, SQL, Opportunity, or Customer) on or after Aug 18, the launch date. Only Inquiry Journeys and Inkwell have usable contact-level tracking right now, see the coverage note below.

tiles.cap: 14 in Inkwell, 2 in Inquiry Journeys. Eight weeks in, on a population of 524 active contacts across the two programs with usable tracking.

tiles.cap: 14 of 108 active contacts, and the strongest movement signal in the portfolio by a wide margin. Inkwell is about a third of IJ's email volume and is producing 7x its lifecycle movement.

tiles.cap: One contact reached MQL, SQL, Opportunity and Customer; a second reached MQL only. IJ carries 71% of all nurture email volume and has produced two lifecycle moves; that gap is still the thing to explain.

tiles.cap: 1 in Inquiry Journeys, one of the two contacts counted in the tile to the left, and 0 in Inkwell. GF8, Agnostic and World History have no usable movement data at all, see Data Coverage.

coverage.title: Data coverage, worth checking against Tim's read
coverage.html: Every metric above comes from four per-product nurture_track contact properties. Two of them are essentially empty: Great First Eight has zero contacts tagged (out of about 78k) despite 405 emails already delivered per the email-analytics view below, and Agnostic has zero as well, despite 469 delivered. That gap points to the workflow sending mail without writing the nurture-track field back to the contact record, or a different, unmapped property holding that data. World History has no contact-level nurture-track property at all. None of this is guesswork on the email side (that data is real and complete); it's specifically the contact-record tracking that's missing for three of the five programs, which is exactly the kind of thing to compare against whatever Tim's exploration turns up.

portfolio.note_html: Eight weeks after the Aug 18 launch, delivery has jumped sharply since the Oct 6 check (9,478 to 12,680), driven mainly by Inquiry Journeys, Inkwell and Great First Eight all crossing module 4 into full send volume for the first time. Agnostic's suppression problem has worsened again: the program now suppresses 142% of what it delivers, up from 130% last week, with module 1 alone now suppressing more than 3x its own delivery. That is worth checking before reading anything else into Agnostic's numbers.

tiles.label: Total delivered across the portfolio, up from 9,478 on Oct 6
tiles.cap: IJ 8,956 · Inkwell 2,850 · GF8 405 · Agnostic 469 · World History 0. Inquiry Journeys alone is 71% of all delivery.

tiles.label: Unique open rate portfolio-wide, bots excluded
tiles.cap: 3,319 unique opens on 12,680 delivered. By program: Inkwell 27.1%, IJ 26.5%, GF8 22.5%, Agnostic 18.6%. Click rate is 1.7% and unsubscribe 0.32%, inside the under-1% guardrail.

tiles.label: Nurture emails that have sent at all
tiles.cap: 16 of the 49 registered emails have no send data yet: all 4 World History emails, modules 7 and 8 across Inquiry Journeys (both tracks, including a duplicate module 7 record), modules 6 through 8 across Inkwell (both tracks), and Agnostic's module 6. The ones showing 1 or 2 sends are test sends, not audience delivery.

tiles.label: Agnostic suppression rate against delivered, the worst in the portfolio
tiles.cap: 666 suppressed against 469 delivered program wide. Module 1 alone suppresses more than 3x what it delivers, 563 suppressed against 186 delivered. Worth checking that track's suppression lists and frequency caps immediately. The cause is not confirmable through the API.

workflows_note_html: Confirmed by Kelsey as the only workflows currently nurturing contacts this fall; everything else in the portal's nurture history is retired. HubSpot's Automation/Workflow objects aren't exposed through the connected API, so enabled/paused state and branch logic still need a manual check in HubSpot, the performance on each card comes from the flow's marketing emails instead.

programs.label: Inquiry Journeys
programs.note_html: Leadership has sent five modules now, four at full volume (1,125, 1,160, 1,079 and 874 delivered) and one still too thin to read (23 on module 5). Classroom has also reached four full-volume modules (1,314, 1,248, 1,178 and 934 delivered); module 5 remains a test send only (2 delivered). Open rate holds in the low-to-high twenties across modules 1 through 4, peaking at 30.8% on Classroom module 3. This program carries 71% of portfolio delivery and has produced two lifecycle stage moves since launch, still the biggest open question on the program.

programs.label: Inkwell
programs.note_html: Still the strongest engagement in the portfolio on open rate (27.1%, best of any program) and the lowest suppression rate by a wide margin (3.8% of delivered, against 20.1% portfolio-wide). Leadership module 4 jumped to the best single open-rate result anywhere this week at 35.4% (74 of 209), narrowly ahead of Leadership module 1's 35.1%. Program-wide unsubscribe sits at 0.49% (14 of 2,850), under the 1% guardrail. Inkwell also accounts for 14 of the 16 lifecycle moves since launch.

programs.label: Great First Eight
programs.note_html: Modules 1 through 4 now all have real volume (128, 118, 89 and 66 delivered); modules 5 and 6 show 2 sends each, which are tests. Clicks are 3 across the whole program, so no reliable click read is possible yet. Unsubscribe reads 0.74% (3 of 405), under the 1% guardrail but still thin enough that one or two people move the number. GF8 still has no contact-level nurture tracking, so none of it reaches the lifecycle section above.

programs.label: Agnostic
programs.note_html: Suppression is now even more dominant: 666 suppressed against 469 delivered program wide, suppressing 142% of what it delivers, up from 130% last week. Module 1 alone suppresses 563 against just 186 delivered, more than 3x its own delivery and sharply worse than last week's ratio. Open rate is 18.6% program wide; module 5 remains the strongest performer at 23.3%, though its volume (30 delivered) is unchanged from last week. Worth checking the suppression lists and frequency caps on this track immediately; the cause is not confirmable from the API.

programs.label: World History
programs.note_html: Unchanged across every check since Aug 31. All four World History emails exist and carry the correct nurture property, but none has ever sent. Two possible causes, neither confirmable through the API: the enrollment audience is empty, or the workflow is not switched on. This program also lacks the nurture_track__world_history contact property entirely, re-checked in HubSpot Oct 13, so it has an enrollment list but no active or exited tracking lists and cannot appear in the lifecycle section above.

emails.note_html: Click-to-open rate (clicks ÷ opens, excluding bots) directly from HubSpot's marketing-email analytics, a purer read on content quality than open rate, since it isolates people who opened and then found something worth clicking. Listed: emails with real volume (20+ delivered as of the last pull); everything thinner is too early to rank. CT = Classroom Track (teacher-facing), LT = Leadership Track (admin-facing).
emails.callout_html: Inkwell's Classroom Track emails continue to convert opens to clicks much better than its Leadership Track (10.5% average CTOR across four CT emails vs. 4.4% across four LT emails, a gap that has narrowed from 3.3x to 2.4x as modules 2 through 4 pick up volume). Inquiry Journeys shows a similar but smaller gap (7.1% CT vs. 4.8% LT), pulled down on both sides by module 4's still-low CTOR now that it has reached full volume for the first time.

audience.role_note_html: Split by the contact's Role property, for the two programs with usable contact-level data. "Admin/Leadership" groups School Leader, District Leader, and Coach/Specialist; "Other/Unassigned" is everyone without a classified role. Both programs look much the same on this cut: roughly half administrators, about a fifth teachers, and the rest unclassified.
audience.source_note_html: Original source (first-touch attribution) for currently-active nurture contacts, IJ and Inkwell.

movement.html: Contacts tagged active/exited in both Inquiry Journeys and Inkwell nurture this season, the only cross-program movement the data shows. GF8 and Agnostic can't be checked for overlap given the tracking gap above; World History has no property to check against.

open_items.html: Inquiry Journeys carries 71% of delivery and has produced two lifecycle moves. 8,956 emails delivered to 416 active contacts, and two contacts account for all of IJ's MQL, SQL, Opportunity and Customer entries since launch. Inkwell, at about a third of IJ's volume, produced 14. This is the biggest open question on the program and it is not an email-performance problem: IJ's open and click rates are healthy.

Agnostic now suppresses significantly more than it delivers, and the gap is widening. Program wide, 666 suppressed against 469 delivered (142%, against 20% portfolio-wide), up from 130% last week. Module 1 alone suppresses more than 3x what it sends (563 suppressed, 186 delivered). Worth checking that track's suppression lists and frequency caps immediately. The cause cannot be confirmed through the API.

Module 4 crossed into real send volume this week across Inquiry Journeys, Inkwell and Great First Eight, all for the first time. Inquiry Journeys Leadership (874 delivered) and Classroom (934), Inkwell Leadership (209) and Classroom (99), and Great First Eight (66) all moved past the 20-delivered test threshold. Module 5 is still mostly thin: Inquiry Journeys Leadership sits at just 23 delivered, and Inkwell and GF8's later modules remain 2-send tests. Agnostic's module 5, which reached real volume last week, held flat at 30 delivered. Modules 6 through 8 in Inquiry Journeys and Inkwell have not sent at all. Eight weeks post launch on a spaced cadence, more volume is still coming in, but most of the portfolio's history is still early modules.

World History has still never sent an email, unchanged since Aug 31: 0 delivered across all 4 emails. Either the enrollment audience is empty or the workflow is not live, and neither is readable via API. Separately, the nurture_track__world_history contact property still does not exist (re-checked Oct 13), so WH has an enrollment list but no active or exited tracking lists. That property sits on Tim's build list and blocks WH from ever appearing in the lifecycle section above.

GF8 and Agnostic still have essentially no contact-level nurture tracking despite actively sending (405 and 469 delivered). Nothing in the lifecycle section can include them. Worth comparing against what Tim's reporting rebuild finds.

Tim's reporting-structure rebuild is still open and is now the binding constraint. It was due Aug 17 and is eight weeks overdue in Asana as of Oct 13. This page is a workaround built from raw API pulls; the Tier 1/2/3 reporting it is standing in for is what the Dec 18 program end and Jan 11 postmortem are supposed to read from.
Confirm enabled/paused state and branch logic for all 5 flows directly in HubSpot. Still not readable via API.

Query note for the next refresh: the nurture_track* properties store the internal value Active, while the display label reads "Active - Inkwell Nurture" and so on per product. Filtering on the label returns zero rows silently. Filter on Active.

footnote_html: Source: HubSpot portal 4451852. CRM contact query API (lifecyclestage v2 stage-entry dates, nurture_track properties) and Marketing Email Analytics API (OVERVIEW, per-email, bots excluded), both pulled Oct 13, 2026, scoped to the 5 confirmed Fall 2026 nurture programs via the nurture property on MARKETING_EMAIL. Lifecycle movement measured from Aug 18, 2026, the launch date recorded on the Asana milestone. Email window Jul 30 to Oct 13, 2026. Active-contact counts are contacts currently tagged Active, so contacts who have exited are not counted. Workflow enabled/paused state is not available via API.
